scope: Genuine provider-derived host first-base worker capability. No socket/channel mount, coupled original-connection bootstrap, readiness/write permission, provider-wide writer stop, full host certificate or Feature07 acceptance. Acceptance remains29/40.
implementation: Only an original retained container lease can mint one non-recyclable worker capability. Private registries retain original grant/data/container ownership, immutable source database path and binding. Caller callbacks, copied facades and serialized descriptions cannot mint it.

Four existing directories are derived from the original source path/incarnation and exact generated backup/stage names. Their original host capabilities remain retained through all three operations, with inode/dev, UID/GID, private mode and canonical identity checks during active and idle use. The original source owns workspace creation/publication.

Canonical fixed requests permit only backup, inspection and verification in that order for one backup. Requests carry no host paths, descriptor numbers, SQL, modules or worker arguments. Invalid or uncertain work closes authority; staged output is preserved.

Unified private task/sandbox resolution retains the existing constructor source context and genuine provider context without caller callbacks. Provider workers force default namespaces even inside trusted hosting; ordinary helpers and constructor source policy retain their contracts.

Linked authority loss invalidates worker admission. Close awaits the original flight and persistent workspace cleanup. A ten-second unsettled close reports uncertainty without discarding the original flight or its retained descriptors; native task scheduler ownership remains until actual task close/cleanup.
